task:
BUILD PART 3 OF 3 OF F2D PR1: the calibration probe, the footprint measurement script and the test seeds over the wide archetype row. Update only the existing branch codex/run-38398470499-1; its head must be fac45d54a1f2607b9bd2327bb00b7c076dcee3e1 -- if it is not, stop and report the SHA you found. Parts 1 and 2 are already on this branch: part 1 rewrote migration 011 to one wide row per system and moved the canonical model to shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py (score_raw_system, VECTOR_READ_SQL, OPPORTUNITY_READ_SQL, confidence_to_ppm, completeness_to_ppm, weighted_key_e4, archetype_model_sha256); part 2 rebuilt the ranking profile and API over it. Read both diffs first (git log -p main..HEAD -- scripts/v3_system_archetype.py shared_contracts/ sql/) so you build on what is actually there, and reuse the part-1 builder for every row you insert.

AUTHORITY: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md. Read CLAUDE.md first, then design sections 3.1-3.4 (columns, indexes, measured footprint), 5.1 (the probe scores through score_raw_system and records archetype_model_sha256), 8.2 (calibration), 8.4 (the capacity gate's footprint-receipt fields -- items (e) and the Arithmetic block), 9 (fixtures and validation lanes) and the PR1 bullet in section 10. Where this task and the design differ, the design wins. Where the design and the current code differ, follow the design and name the conflict in your summary. Do not reopen design decisions.

SCOPE. This part completes PR1. After it lands, every suite on the branch should pass on the disposable PostgreSQL 18 lanes (Backend integration, Script contracts + migration paths, Canonical safety, Review Lab, Cypress) -- so besides the files below, fix any test on the branch that still assumes the old keyed system_archetype table or the physical system_archetype_summary table, by making it assert the wide-row contract (never by skipping, xfailing or deleting it). PR2 work stays out: no migration 015, no PUBLISHED-base acceptance in the builders, no published_at requirement in the API, no product publication in the seeds. Do not touch apps/api/src/ranking/*, apps/api/src/routers/*, apps/api/src/models.py, apps/api/src/local_search.py, sql/v3/migrations/011_v3_system_archetype.sql, shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py or scripts/v3_system_archetype.py except to fix a defect that blocks this part, and name any such change in your summary.

ALLOWED FILES: scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py; scripts/dev/measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py; scripts/dev/seed_v3_fixture_generation.py; scripts/dev/seed_cypress_v3_generation.py; scripts/dev/review_lab/*.py only where it writes or checks archetype rows or the summary table; scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh only if its pending-set contract pins the 011 hash; tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py, tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe_operator.py, tests/test_measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py, tests/test_measure_wide_archetype_probe_indexes.py, the two seed test modules, tests/test_review_lab_v3.py, tests/integration/conftest.py, tests/ratings_v4_pg_fixture.py; any other test on the branch that still assumes the old archetype shape (list each one in your summary with the assumption it made); CHANGES.md. Any other changed path must be justified in your summary as required by a specific failing test, otherwise it is a failure.

CALIBRATION PROBE (design sections 5.1 and 8.2). scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py currently scales vectors itself and calls model.fit_all (around line 99). Change it to read raw rows through the model's two shared SQL constants (VECTOR_READ_SQL with the system or chunk parameters, OPPORTUNITY_READ_SQL returning count(*)::int and sum(local_score)::bigint) and score each system through score_raw_system -- no private copy of the scaling, no SQL avg, no reimplementation of the opportunity mean or the ppm rounding. Record archetype_model_sha256 (from the canonical module) and model_file_sha256 in the probe receipt beside the existing code identity and coefficients, so the capacity gate of section 8.4 item (b) can compare them. Emit per-archetype S/A/B/C/D tier counts under per_archetype.<key>.tier_histogram and the probe's row count, in the shape section 8.4's "Histogram conversion" paragraph consumes (the converter script itself is PR4; do not write it). Keep the probe read-only and keep every existing fail-closed check and exit code. Tests: the probe's scores for a fixture row equal score_raw_system on the same raw row; the receipt carries both digests; a module-level assertion that the probe source contains no private scaling (no '/ 10_000' or 'fit_all(' call) and no SQL avg(.

FOOTPRINT MEASUREMENT (design sections 3.4, 8.4 item (e), 10 PR1 bullet). scripts/dev/measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py gains a --migration-sql <path> mode that: applies the given final 011 migration text to the disposable database (with the prerequisite migrations it needs, exactly as the existing archetype tests build their fixture); creates every index on the empty relation (the migration already does); then fills the real v3_derived.system_archetype table in canonical chunk order through the part-1 builder's insert path (not a private INSERT), using a synthetic score distribution shaped by --fractions-json {<key>: {"60": f, "76": f, "88": f}} when given, else the script's declared built-in synthetic distribution; runs VACUUM ANALYZE; sizes the heap and all 26 indexes individually with pg_table_size / pg_relation_size; and emits a receipt with heap_bytes_per_row, primary_key_bytes_per_row, weighted_index_bytes_per_row and tier_index_bytes_per_row_per_unit_fraction, each computed from unrounded bytes with the round-up rule (ceil), where the tier figure is the summed bytes of the 24 partials divided by the row count and by the receipt's own sigma_all (the sum of the 24 per-key fractions it actually seeded), plus: the sha256 of the applied 011 text, fractions_sha256 (canonical sorted-key JSON of the fractions used), score_distribution_source ('synthetic-builtin' or 'measured-histogram' when --fractions-json was given), sigma_all, row count, per-index bytes, and capacity_gate_eligible, which is true only when the final-migration path ran AND score_distribution_source is 'measured-histogram'. The committed built-in layouts (v1..v4) stay as the pre-migration reference and the default mode is unchanged. PR1's own committed receipt, if you produce one, must use the declared synthetic distribution and be labelled capacity_gate_eligible: false. The f2d_operator_code_sha256 field is PR4's; leave a documented placeholder key absent rather than inventing a value. Tests (disposable PG18 where needed, pure where possible): the tier figure is normalised by the receipt's own sigma_all (two fixtures with different fractions give the same per-unit-fraction value within rounding); each of the four per-row figures is ceil of unrounded bytes / rows; capacity_gate_eligible is false for the built-in distribution and true for a fractions file; the 011 hash in the receipt equals sha256 of the file applied; the receipt refuses to be written if any of the 26 indexes is missing after the fill; --fractions-json with a key missing or f60 < f76 is rejected.

SEEDS (design section 9; PR1 bullet). scripts/dev/seed_v3_fixture_generation.py and scripts/dev/seed_cypress_v3_generation.py write wide rows through the part-1 builder (register -> build -> validate) rather than any direct insert into the old keyed table, and no longer reference v3_derived.system_archetype_summary as a physical table (seed_v3_fixture_generation.py line 50-51 checks to_regclass('v3_derived.system_archetype_summary') -- change it to the wide table and the v3_app.system_archetype_summary view). Both products reach READY as today; product publication waits for PR2. Review Lab and Cypress lanes consume these seeds, so run their seed test modules.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: ruff check scripts tests; python -m pytest tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe_operator.py tests/test_measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py tests/test_measure_wide_archetype_probe_indexes.py -q -p no:warnings; the two seed test modules and tests/test_review_lab_v3.py; then the WHOLE tests/ directory once with -q -p no:warnings and report passed/failed/skipped counts, listing every failure that remains and whether it needs a database (runners have no PostgreSQL; database tests skip or fail locally and run in CI). Do not deploy, contact production, or use production credentials.

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING IN THIS SESSION, complete in this order and stop cleanly: seeds, calibration probe, footprint --migration-sql, remaining old-shape test fixes. State precisely what remains. End with: files changed; tests run with counts; database tests written but not run; every test you changed because it assumed the old shape; and any design-versus-code conflict you found.
